options: A centralised repository that stores structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its raw form
A normalised relational database for transactions
A department-level analytical mart
A virtual layer over source systems
A pre-aggregated multidimensional cube
questions.explanation: A data lake is a centralised repository that stores structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its raw form.

questions.stem: What challenge led to the emergence of the data lake?
options: Data warehouses were too expensive to license
Warehouses handled structured data well but were not designed to ingest, store or process semi-structured and unstructured data at scale
OLTP systems could not process transactions fast enough
Regulators demanded raw data retention
Relational databases stopped supporting SQL
questions.explanation: The digital economy produced clickstreams, social posts, sensor readings, videos, documents and logs, which made up most enterprise data, yet traditional warehouses could not handle them at scale.

questions.stem: What does the schema-on-read philosophy of a data lake mean?
options: Data must be modelled and cleansed before it is loaded
Data is ingested quickly without upfront modelling, and structure is applied later when it is analysed
Only data with a predefined schema can be read
Schemas are read from the source system's catalogue
Data is encrypted before reading
questions.explanation: Unlike a warehouse, which requires modelling before loading, a data lake ingests data without upfront modelling and applies structure later at analysis time.

questions.stem: On which storage technologies does a data lake architecture typically rest?
options: Tape libraries and optical discs
HDFS in its early days and, more recently, cloud object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage or Google Cloud Storage
Relational databases such as Oracle and SQL Server
In-memory caches such as Redis
Spreadsheets shared on a network drive
questions.explanation: Data lakes were built on HDFS early on and now on cloud object storage platforms such as Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage and Google Cloud Storage.

questions.stem: Why did data lake storage make it feasible to retain information that was once discarded?
options: Because it compresses data to zero
Because it holds massive volumes of diverse data at low cost, even data that does not fit a relational schema
Because it deletes duplicates automatically
Because regulators pay for the storage
Because it only stores summaries
questions.explanation: These systems hold massive volumes of diverse data at low cost, so information that did not fit neatly into a relational schema no longer had to be discarded.

questions.stem: In the healthcare example, which data type is described as semi-structured?
options: Patient records
Billing data
XML-based lab results
X-ray and MRI images
Physician notes
questions.explanation: Hospitals generate structured data (patient records, billing), semi-structured data (XML-based lab results) and unstructured data (X-rays, MRI images, physician notes).

questions.stem: In the healthcare data lake example, which technique is applied to doctors' notes?
options: Computer vision
Statistical analysis
Natural language processing
Schema-on-write modelling
Referential integrity checks
questions.explanation: Analysts apply natural language processing to doctors' notes, computer vision to radiology images and statistical analysis to lab data, all within the same environment.

options: A data lake stored on-premises rather than in the cloud
A data lake that has degraded into a repository where data is plentiful but poorly catalogued, inconsistent and hard to use
A data lake that contains only structured data
A backup copy of a data lake
A data lake with too little data
questions.explanation: Without careful management a data lake can degrade into a data swamp, where data is plentiful but poorly catalogued, inconsistent and hard to use.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the practices modern data lake implementations emphasise to preserve usability?
options: Metadata management
Data catalogues
Access controls
Lifecycle governance
Mandatory upfront 3NF modelling
questions.explanation: Modern lakes emphasise metadata management, data catalogues, access controls and lifecycle governance; mandatory upfront modelling contradicts the schema-on-read approach.

questions.stem: How does a data lake relate to a data warehouse?
options: It replaces the warehouse entirely
It complements the warehouse by addressing new forms of information and supporting advanced analytics, machine learning and real-time decision-making
It is a smaller subset of the warehouse
It is the same thing under a new name
It is a warehouse without any governance
questions.explanation: The data lake complements the data warehouse by handling new data forms and supporting advanced analytics, machine learning and real-time decisions.
